We focus on evaluating informativeness and diversity of summary sentences. For informativeness, we take the union of summary sentences and ask human evaluators to judge the relevance of each sentence against the ground-truth summary on a scale of 1 (worst) to 5 (best). For diversity, we obtain the symmetric difference of two summaries and ask humans to judge if each sentence has offered new content different from those of the common sentences.
